key_insight: Split complex-valued PINNs improve accuracy and phase representation by learning real and imaginary components separately, reducing spectral bias on oscillatory nonlinear PDEs.
engineering_relevance: This makes PINNs more reliable for fluid mechanics and wave-dominated systems where capturing sharp gradients, oscillations, and hidden parameters is critical.
method: Use complex-valued network weights and latent states
Apply standard real activations separately to real and imaginary parts
Train on physics residuals for forward and inverse PDEs with collocation points
evidence_signal: The paper benchmarks SCV-PINN on many forward and inverse PDEs and flow problems, reporting consistently lower relative L2 error, including 4.07e-5 on the 3D Navier-Stokes Beltrami case.
watch_item: Complex-valued training and collocation design may add implementation sensitivity, so gains can depend on activation choice, sampling strategy, and problem scaling.
paper_title: Split Complex-Valued Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Forward and Inverse Nonlinear PDEs
